messages.author: ecca3e70149d98bf
messages.subject: installing the NicheMapR package - gfortran version
parts:
Hi Mike,

I have been struggling with installing the NicheMapR on my new laptop. One of the errors I get states
"ld: warning: search path '/opt/gfortran/lib/gcc/aarch64-apple-darwin20.0/12.2.0' not found
ld: library 'gfortran' not found"
This path is exactly where it should be looking, but I have a newer version of gfortran (14.2.0_1).
Is there a way I should tell R to look for a newer version of gfortran? Or do you recommend installing an older version of gfortran?

Gratefully,
Tom Radomski

Hi Hediyeh,
The error indicates that it can't find the fortran compiler, so the problem is with how you're installing fortran " /opt/gfortran/bin/gfortran: No such file or directory"
Googling that error I got to this page which you can have a look at and try out or see if you can find other solutions.
All the best,
Mike

Dear Mac users,
If you've had trouble compilling NicheMapR, make sure you've got the right version of R for your chip (Intel vs am64 silicon) - R will still run if it's the wrong version but won't compile Fortran properly. Also, get the correct version of gfortran from here
All the best,
Mike

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: installing the NicheMapR package - gfortran version
parts:
And Dan Noble has made these notes for OSX (thanks Dan)

# 1. Install gfortran using homebrew in the terminal/bash window
   brew install gcc
# 2. Take note of the path to gfortran. You'll need this for later
    which gfortran

# 3. In home directory of terminal create a Makevars file
   mkdir ~/.R
   touch ~/.R/Makevars
   open  ~/.R/Makevars

# 4. Add the following to the Makevars file. Note that you need to make sure your version of fortran is correct and replace 124.2.0_1 with your version. You can find version in terminal by typing `gfortran --version`. In addition you need to replace the path to gfortran with the path you found in step 2.
    FC = /opt/homebrew/Cellar/gcc/14.2.0_1/bin/gfortran
   F77 = /opt/homebrew/Cellar/gcc/14.2.0_1/bin/gfortran
 FLIBS = -L/opt/homebrew/Cellar/gcc/14.2.0_1/lib/gcc/11

#5. Restart R and try to install the package again via devtools. It should now work.
